issues.description: Chapter should explain that ripgrep searches directories recursively by default
issues.should_add: Explanation that when you provide a directory path as an argument, ripgrep automatically descends into all subdirectories (unless limited by --max-depth or ignore files)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section explaining: 'When you specify a directory as a search path, ripgrep will recursively search all files within that directory and its subdirectories. For example, `rg pattern dir/` will search all files under dir/.'
issues.source_reference: rg --help output: 'ripgrep (rg) recursively searches the current directory', 'A file or directory to search. Directories are searched recursively.'

issues.description: Chapter should document the --max-depth/-d flag for controlling recursion depth
issues.should_add: Documentation of --max-depth NUM flag (short form: -d) and its alias --maxdepth
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section explaining --max-depth: 'Limit the depth of directory traversal. A value of 0 only searches the explicitly given paths themselves (no recursion). A value of 1 searches only the direct children of the given directory. For example, `rg --max-depth 0 dir/` is a no-op because dir/ will not be descended into. `rg --max-depth 1 dir/` will search only the direct children of dir/.'

issues.description: Chapter should explain how file vs directory paths are handled differently
issues.should_add: Explanation of how ripgrep handles file paths (searches the file directly) vs directory paths (recursive search)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section: 'ripgrep treats file and directory paths differently. File paths specified on the command line are searched directly and override glob/ignore rules. Directory paths trigger recursive traversal. You can mix both: `rg pattern file.txt dir/` searches file.txt directly and recursively searches dir/.'
issues.source_reference: rg --help: 'File paths specified on the command line override glob and ignore rules', crates/ignore/src/walk.rs:WalkBuilder

issues.description: Chapter should explain the traversal mechanism and parallel walking
issues.should_add: High-level explanation of how ripgrep walks directories (using WalkBuilder and parallel traversal)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add technical background: 'ripgrep uses an efficient parallel directory walker that respects ignore files. The walker is configured with options like max_depth, follow_links, same_file_system, and integrates with the ignore file system to skip filtered paths during traversal.'

issues.description: Chapter should document -L/--follow flag for following symbolic links during traversal
issues.should_add: Documentation of -L/--follow flag and its interaction with recursive search
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section: 'By default, ripgrep does not follow symbolic links to directories. Use -L/--follow to enable following symlinks during recursive directory traversal. Be careful with -L as it can cause infinite loops if symlinks create cycles.'

issues.should_add: Documentation of --one-file-system flag to restrict traversal to a single file system
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section: 'Use --one-file-system to prevent ripgrep from crossing file system boundaries during recursive search. This is useful when searching from the root directory to avoid traversing mounted file systems.'
